text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - London's FTSE 100 share index ended higher on Thursday after creeping tentatively upwards in the wake of a rejuvenated Dow, but fears of another reversal on Wall Street capped the FTSE's gains and kept volume subdued. The blue-chip index ended 20.9 points higher at 4,228.4. FRANKFURT - German shares gained ground in early dealings on Thursday as the DAX index hurdled the 3,000 point level and held onto the gains to end bourse trade higher.
The 30-share DAX index ended up 18.12 points at 3,017.32 points, buoyed by gains in DAX heavyweight Allianz AG.
In post-bourse trade the index stood at 3,018.58. up 20.63.

PARIS - French stocks rallied to historic highs on Thursday, propelling the blue-chip CAC-40 index above 2,500 points for the first time, after the Bank of France trimmed its leading intervention rate.

The CAC-40 index finished up 38.05 points, or 1.54 percent, at 2,503.06, boosted by a 15.53 percent surge in shares of electrical engineering group Alcatel Alsthom, which said it expected to show net income of 2.5 billion francs for 1996. Analysts were expecting a profit closer to 1.4 billion.

ZURICH - Swiss indices posted record closing highs in very high volume, pulled up by Wall Street gains and strong demand for pharmaceuticals. Major banks underperformed the market, which may have been triggered by fears the Swiss banks may face a ban in New York, a dealer noted.

The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) firmed 39.2 points, or 0.94 percent, at 4,208.9 points, a shade off the all-time high at 4,215.4 points. The broad Swiss Market Index (SPI) ended up 22.75 points, or 0.85 percent, to 2,689.38.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's rally over the past two days fizzled on Thursday, as the key market index lost close to 500 points, hurt by lingering worries about the banking sector.
The market's benchmark index, Nikkei 225 average, dropped by 471.26 points, or 2.57 percent, to end at 17,864.04. It fell as low as 17,781.89 at one point.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended flat on Thursday, unable to retain the momentum of an early rally as property issues remained depressed and concerns about interest rates continued to dampen sentiment.
The Hang Seng Index rose 2.97 points, or 0.02 percent, to 13,288.40 after touching an early high of 13,405.54.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed just firmer on Thursday, the market sliding off its highs in the afternoon as bellwether BHP faded amid heavy options trade as the January series options reached expiry.
The All Ordinaries index rose 3.5 points at 2,417.7.

JOHANNESBURG - Snubbing heady gains on Wall Street on Wednesday night, South African shares drooped in futures-led activity on Thursday. Gold shares were further pressured by bullion which hovered weakly below the $350 level.
Traders said industrial stocks were given a respite early in the afternoon when buying interest, from both local players and offshore, materialised.
However, most of these gains were erased towards the close with the industrial 100 percent index ending 48.4 points weaker at 7,962.6.
An improved rand continued to be the thorn in the flesh of gold stocks, also good rand-hedges, with the gold index losing almost 1.5 percent on a sickly bullion price.
The all gold 100 index lost 19.8 points to 1,365.7 and the overall market index ended 29.3 points down at 6,658.2
